findings.title: forEach(async) detaches calendar/video cancellation and disables the try/catch
findings.body: The callback passed to bookingRefsFiltered.forEach is now async and awaits getCalendar, but Array.prototype.forEach ignores the returned promise. Consequences: (1) the try/catch at lines 124-139 can no longer catch anything. getCalendar, deleteEvent and deleteMeeting failures become unhandled promise rejections, which crash Node by default on v15+. (2) Reschedule returns true before the calendar and video cancellations have run, so the booking is marked cancelled while the old calendar slot may still be held. Fix by using a for...of loop with await inside the existing try block.

findings.title: forEach(async) detaches calendar/video cancellation and disables the try/catch
findings.body: Same defect as the vital reschedule: the forEach callback is async and awaits getCalendar, but forEach does not await it. The surrounding try/catch no longer sees errors from getCalendar or deleteEvent/deleteMeeting, which become unhandled rejections. The function also returns true before the cancellations finish. Use for...of with await so the existing try/catch and ordering actually apply.

findings.title: Unawaited async forEach in requestReschedule drops errors and races the response
findings.body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach now takes an async callback that awaits getCalendar and then calls deleteEvent/deleteMeeting. forEach does not await these promises, and this block has no try/catch. The mutation proceeds to sendRequestRescheduleEmail and returns while calendar and video deletions are still in flight. Any rejection (credential failure, network error) becomes an unhandled promise rejection instead of a handled error. Replace with for...of and await each deletion, or collect the promises and Promise.allSettled them.

findings.title: Calendar deletions in an unawaited forEach(async) are never awaited and their errors are lost
findings.body: The recurring-cancel branch calls bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { ... await getCalendar(credential) ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) }). This PR adds an await ahead of the loop, so every push happens later. The handler snapshots apiDeletes at line 652 (prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) and awaits only that copy, so these deletions are neither awaited nor reflected in the response. Cancellation can return success before calendar events are removed, and any rejection is an unhandled rejection. Use for...of with await and push into apiDeletes before the final Promise.all.

findings.title: import() calls are evaluated eagerly, so the modules are not actually deferred
findings.body: Each entry is written as a direct import("./x") call inside the object literal. Those calls run when index.ts is evaluated, so every app module still starts loading on the first import of @calcom/app-store, just without blocking. The only change is that the module evaluation no longer blocks synchronously. If the goal is lazy loading, each entry should be a function such as () => import("./x") that consumers invoke only when needed. As written, the PR does not reduce load work or startup cost.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials stores un-awaited getCalendar promises in a sync function
findings.body: getCalendarCredentials is still synchronous, but getCalendar is now async, so the calendar field of each returned entry is a Promise<Calendar | null>. Only getConnectedCalendars awaits it (line 48). Any other consumer that uses the field as a Calendar will fail to typecheck, and any rejection from getCalendar (for example a CalendarService constructor throw) in an entry that is never awaited becomes an unhandled rejection. The return type should make the Promise explicit, or the function should become async and its callers should await it.

findings.title: Sync-to-async signature changes have no test updates
findings.body: getCalendar changes from a synchronous return to Promise<Calendar | null>, and deleteMeeting, deleteEvent, getVideoAdapters and about 12 call sites across 10 files gain awaits. The PR touches no test files. Existing unit tests that stub getCalendar, deleteMeeting or appStore synchronously will break or silently pass against the wrong shape. The unhandled-rejection problems in the forEach call sites would also go undetected because no test exercises the failure paths of these functions.
